title: Inverse trigonometric functions and their derivatives
goal: Differentiate inverse trig functions ($\arcsin, \arccos, \arctan, \operatorname{arcsec}$) and find the slope of an inverse function $f^{-1}$ by flipping the slope of $f$.

beforeThis.skill: Intuition: an inverse function swaps $x$ and $y$, so its graph is flipped across $y = x$ and its slope is the reciprocal $\frac{1}{f'(x)}$!

links.label: Precalculus: Trigonometry and inverse trig domains

seeIt.title: The Derivative of Trigonometric Functions
seeIt.creator: Dr. Trefor Bazett
seeIt.watchFor: Reviews trigonometric derivatives and right-triangle relationships used in inverse trig differentiation.

questions.asking: Find the derivative $f'(x)$ of $\arcsin(x/3)$ and state the interval of $x$-values for which $f(x)$ is defined.
Find the derivative $f'(t)$ and state all $t$-values in $[-1, 1]$ where the denominator $t^2 - 1$ is nonzero.
questions.statement: Differentiate $f(t) = \dfrac{\arccos t}{t^2 - 1}$. What is the domain of $f(t)$?

questions.asking: Use the chain rule on $\operatorname{arcsec}(u)$ and check which real numbers $x$ satisfy $|-x^2 - 2| \ge 1$.
Use the chain rule $(\arctan u)' = \frac{u'}{1 + u^2}$ with $u = x/a$ and simplify the complex fraction.
questions.statement: Differentiate $f(x) = \dfrac{1}{a} \arctan\left(\dfrac{x}{a}\right)$, where $a$ is a nonzero constant. What is the domain of $f(x)$?

questions.asking: Use the product rule on $x \arcsin x$ and the chain rule on $\sqrt{1 - x^2}$—watch how neatly the two parts cancel!
questions.statement: Differentiate $f(x) = x \arcsin x + \sqrt{1 - x^2}$. What is the domain of $f(x)$?

questions.asking: Differentiate $\arctan(x^2)$ using the chain rule, set the numerator equal to $0$, and solve for $x$.
questions.statement: For which values of $x$ is the tangent line to $y = \arctan(x^2)$ horizontal?

questions.asking: Add the derivatives of $\arcsin x$ and $\arccos x$ together—notice why their sum is $0$ (geometrically, $\arcsin x + \arccos x = \pi/2$ is a constant!).
Express the derivative $g'(y)$ of the inverse function $g(y) = f^{-1}(y)$ when $f(x) = x + \cos x$.
questions.statement: Let $f(x) = x + \cos x$, and let $g(y) = f^{-1}(y)$ be the inverse function. Determine $g'(y)$.

questions.asking: Find the exact numerical value of the derivative of the inverse function $f^{-1}$ at the output $y = \pi - 1$ by first identifying which input $x$ gives $f(x) = \pi - 1$.
Find the exact numerical value of the derivative of the inverse function $f^{-1}$ at the output $y = e + 1$ by first identifying which input $x$ gives $f(x) = e + 1$.
Differentiate both sides of $\arcsin(x + 2y) = x^2 + y^2$ with respect to $x$ and solve for $y'$ in terms of $x$ and $y$.
questions.statement:
Suppose a curve is defined implicitly by

$$\arcsin(x + 2y) = x^2 + y^2.$$

Solve for $y'$ in terms of $x$ and $y$.
